bugs.root_cause: attrs.converters.optional() wraps a Converter returned by pipe(str, int) in a plain single-argument closure. The generated __init__ therefore calls optional_converter(value), and optional_converter calls the inner Converter with only value even though the Converter requires value, instance, and field. This causes a TypeError when Measurement("42") is constructed.

impacted_items.reason: This is the function containing the bug; optional() incorrectly handles a Converter object returned by pipe().
pipe() returns a Converter requiring value, instance, and field, which is incompatible with the current optional() wrapper.
The Converter call requires three arguments, but optional_converter currently supplies only the value.
It correctly wraps the plain optional_converter, but this wrapping exposes the incompatible single-argument call path.
This module re-exports optional from attr.converters, so the namespace is affected when the underlying implementation is fixed.
This is a namespace import with no converter logic of its own.

bugs.root_cause: ExpenseTracker.update_expense (api.py line 87-88) calls self.get_expense(expense_id), which returns None when the ID is not found. The very next line dereferences exp.title (if exp.title is None:) without first checking whether exp itself is None. This raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'title' instead of the intended ValueError('Expense ... not found.'). The fix is to guard with `if exp is None:` before touching any attribute of exp.

impacted_items.reason: This is the bug site; the missing None-check causes AttributeError to propagate to every caller instead of a clean ValueError.
get_expense correctly returns None for a missing ID, but the caller (update_expense) fails to handle that None return value.
cmd_update is the CLI entry point that calls update_expense; it propagates the uncaught AttributeError directly to the user as a raw traceback.
Existing test accepts both ValueError and AttributeError (`pytest.raises((ValueError, AttributeError))`), so it passes even with the bug present and provides weak coverage.

bugs.root_cause: ExpenseTracker.over_budget_categories (api.py line 221) filters by s["percent_used"] > 100, but percent_used is computed as round(spent / monthly_limit * 100, 1) in budget_status (utils.py line 126). Python's banker's rounding causes round(100.1, 1) to evaluate to 100.0, so 100.0 > 100 is False and a category spending $100.01 against a $100.00 limit is silently excluded from the over-budget list. Meanwhile budget_status already computes the exact boolean over_budget: remaining < 0 (no rounding), which is True for $100.01 spent. The fix is to filter by s["over_budget"] directly instead of re-deriving from the rounded percent_used.

impacted_items.reason: This is the bug site; the wrong predicate (percent_used > 100) loses categories that are genuinely over budget due to rounding.
Computes both percent_used (rounded, lossy) and over_budget (exact, correct); the over_budget field is the authoritative source that over_budget_categories should use.
Correctly assembles and returns the list of status dicts from budget_status; its output already contains the accurate over_budget field.
CLI caller of check_all_budgets and check_budget; already reads status["over_budget"] via _print_budget, so it is unaffected by the fix to over_budget_categories.

bugs.root_cause: to_csv_rows in utils.py was declared with headers: List[str] = []. Python evaluates default argument expressions exactly once at function-definition time, so every call that omits headers shares the same list object. Any code that obtained a reference to that shared default and mutated it (via extend, append, or +=) would corrupt all subsequent headerless calls, which would then receive the already-mutated list instead of the canonical six-column default. The fix is to use headers: Optional[List[str]] = None and guard internally with `row_headers = headers if headers is not None else default_headers`.

impacted_items.reason: This is the bug site; the mutable default list is shared across all callers, making the function's output silently depend on call-site mutation history.
Calls to_csv_rows(expenses) with no headers argument; if the shared default is mutated by another caller earlier in the process, export_csv silently produces a wrong header row in the output file.
Calls export_csv which calls to_csv_rows without headers; inherits the corruption risk from export_csv and exposes it to every consumer of the API.

CLI entry point that calls export_to_csv; a corrupted header would silently appear in the output CSV file with no error raised, but cmd_export has no direct interaction with the default list object itself.
